properties.name: Where measurement shows adjacency work is the cost, reflow2's graph engine keeps one compact index per primitive — edge types interned, symmetric relations stored once, inverses computed from the declared algebra — derived from the stored graph, never written as a second copy
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-28, in a dev_reflow2 session: "let's go with idea 4, the 1, 2, and 3" — promoting dec:idea-store-each-primitive-as-its-own-compact-index from the graph-primitives design on flo2 (graph 85a2a1a36e7c942d).
properties.statement:
THIRD of the four performance requirements Anthony promoted on 2026-09-28. GATED on req:time-and-tokens-are-measured-per-task-against-budgets: built where that measurement shows adjacency scans or edge-type comparison miss a budget, not before.
(a) A compressed-sparse-row adjacency per primitive, built from the declared readings at load or refresh, so a one-kind projection is an existing array rather than a filter over every edge.
(b) Edge-type names and property keys interned to small integers in hot paths (cheapest; may be worth doing regardless).
(c) Using the declared algebra (req:every-relationship-declares-its-algebra-and-no-method-runs-where-it-cannot-represent-it): a symmetric relation stored once, an inverse pair stored one way, a declared composition computed rather than stored.
(d) Hot bulk-read fields held as columns — last, and only if measured.
Every index is DERIVED from the stored graph and rebuilt from it; it is never written independently, because a second copy that can drift is what test 2(i) of the true-knowledge-graph definition forbids.

Counter-argument carried from the brainstorm: at reflow2's sizes algorithms already run in milliseconds, and its recorded wins (hydrate 8.8 s → 0.9 s, defect sweep 44.5 s → 4.4 s) came from whole-graph passes and redundant work, not adjacency layout — the gate exists for exactly that reason.
